question: In suspected infective endocarditis, at least three sets of blood cultures drawn from separate venepuncture sites over 30–60 minutes should be obtained BEFORE starting antimicrobial therapy, except in haemodynamically unstable patients.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Three separate blood culture sets (different venepuncture sites, at least 30 minutes apart) before antibiotics is the standard. This is essential because the organism drives the antimicrobial choice and duration. Only severe haemodynamic compromise justifies skipping this step.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Blood cultures before antibiotics is a cardinal rule in IE. The yield of blood cultures drops dramatically after even a single antibiotic dose — making organism identification (which determines the antibiotic regimen and duration) impossible. Haemodynamic instability (cardiogenic shock, valve rupture) is the only justification for starting antibiotics before completing cultures.
